https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/16/ukra.text: Ukrainian drones forced all four of Moscow's main airports to close overnight, with Vnukovo, Domodedovo, Zhukovsky and Sheremetyevo suspended for up to seven hours and more than 160 flights cancelled.Moscow mayor Sergei Sobyanin said 94 drones heading towards the capital had been shot down.Pulkovo airport in St Petersburg was twice forced to halt operations during the same night. Governor of Leningrad region Alexander Drozdenko said four drones were destroyed over the region.Euronews could not independently verify the claims.According to Russian investigative outlet Agentstvo, Moscow's four airports were closed for a total of 101 hours in the first 14 days of October, compared with 46 hours across the whole of September.On Tuesday, Ukraine carried out one of its largest drone operations against the Russian capital, deploying close to 500 drones.On 9 October, according to multiple reports, the presidential aircraft carrying Vladimir Putin — returning from a summit in Turkmenistan — was unable to land in Moscow due to a drone attack and was diverted to St Petersburg. Putin's plane was not reported to have been a direct target.Russian officials have neither confirmed nor denied the reports.Ukraine has not officially confirmed any organised campaign to shut down Russian airports, in what media outlets have dubbed "Operation M&Ms".President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has not yet authorised the military to proceed with an original, more aggressive plan for such a campaign, according to reports.In September, Zelenskyy said Russian skies "are becoming unsafe" and that "drones will appear in the skies over Russia, and that will have to be taken into account", urging international airlines to stop flying to Russian airports.Kyiv has targeted Russia's military, energy and commercial facilities in a bid to defund Moscow's war machine, as its all-out war in Ukraine continued well into its fifth year.Yet US President Donald Trump reiterated criticism of Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries in an interview, calling them "a disgrace" after his shock announcement of a deal to purchase diesel from the Kremlin."There are many targets that can be hit. But when you shell oil refineries that produce, you know, diesel fuel, and we and the whole world need that, (Zelenskyy) is not doing the world a favour," Trump said.

https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cr3e.text: Image source, EPA Image caption, RosalÃ­a released her fourth album Lux last year to rave reviews By Riyah Collins BBC Newsbeat Published 13 November 2026 Spanish star RosalÃ­a has made history as the first woman to win the best album award at the Latin Grammys three times, after being recognised for her project Lux. The singer took home five trophies in total, including two for her track La Perla which was named song of the year and best pop song. La Perla was also nominated for record of the year but missed out to Argentine singer Milo J's song NiÃ±o. RosalÃ­a released Lux last year to rave reviews and collecting her award at the ceremony in Las Vegas on Thursday, she said: "To all the people who told me I wasn't good enough, or that my music was too weird, I'm thankful I didn't listen." The Barcelona-born artist then added: "Now I'm winning these prizes." RosalÃ­a, who opened the ceremony with a performance of some of her biggest songs, was honoured with the prize for best alternative music album. She also picked up best shortform music video for her track Sauvignon Blanc. The singer had previously won best album for El Mal Querer in 2019 and Motomami in 2022 - and her third Lux is also tipped to be a favourite when nominations are announced for the Grammys next week. Image source, Getty Images Image caption, After a career spanning three decades, Daddy Yankee was recognised with a lifetime achievement award It was also a big night for Puerto Rican reggaeton legend Daddy Yankee, who won the person of the year award. He performed some of his best-loved tracks including Gasolina and Con Calma, and was joined on stage by rappers including LL Cool J and French Montana. Punjabi singer Diljit Dosanjh, who collabed with Daddy Yankee on Pokito, even took a break from his Aura India tour for the set, making him the first Indian artist to perform at the Latin Grammys. Dosanjh superfan Devanshi Arora described the singer's appearance as "a cultural revolution". "It's really invigorating and motivating to see someone from my country has made it all around the world," she tells Newsbeat. She sees a lot of similarities between South American and Punjabi communities and hopes this leads to more collaborations - with a link-up between Dosanjh and Bad Bunny top of her wishlist. Daddy Yankee was presented with the lifetime achievement award by Janet Jackson, who told him in Spanish that his music "has inspired an entire generation". Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Diljit Dosanjh became the first Indian artist to perform at the Latin Grammys Accepting the prize for record of the year, Milo J seemed surprised to have won ahead of strong competition from Karol G, Jorge Drexler, Carin LeÃ³n as well as RosalÃ­a. The 20-year-old took home four trophies in the end and gave a shout out to Argentine folk music. He described NiÃ±o as the song "I'm most proud of out of everything I've created so far". "Long live Argentine folk music," he added. Elsewhere, ARIA VEGA was named best new artist and songwriter of the year went to Sara Schell.
